hypothesis: Blind normal faults in the Basin and Range extend beyond their mapped surface traces at depth. The USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue maps surface traces only; blind extensions are missing from it. Targeting h19_5 skeleton termini (fault-trace endpoints) within 6 px, off the catalogue (d_cat > 2.0 px), in the productive 2-6 px catalogue band, recovers blind extensions that are geologically continuous with mapped faults but absent from the catalogue.
mechanism: S = exp(-d_endpoint / 3.0) restricted to footprint & ~catalogue & (d_cat > 2.0) & (d_endpoint <= 6) & ~h19_5, where d_endpoint is the Euclidean distance transform from h19_5 8-connectivity endpoints and d_cat is the catalogue distance transform. 37,654 dots selected by score-ranked non-maximum suppression at >= 2.83 px (~300 m, the DTI triangular-kernel radius). Pure array math on bridge masks; the catalogue is used only for masking, never to build features.
named_non_fault_mimic: Mapped-fault splays and tip damage zones that are already in the catalogue (excluded by d_cat > 2.0); non-tectonic linear features (alluvial fan distributary channels, playa shorelines) that happen to lie near skeleton endpoints (partially mitigated by the d_endpoint reach limit and the off-catalogue requirement).
